items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, Economics or related field or an equivalent combination of education and experience
Experience preparing financial reports, reconciling accounts, and maintaining accurate financial records
Professional accounting or finance experience in higher education, healthcare, research, nonprofit, or public-sector environments
Experience reviewing and processing financial transactions with strong attention to detail
Experience using institutional systems such as UCPath, OFC/OASIS, QDB, or similar enterprise financial platforms

The Semel Institute for Neuroscience and Human Behavior is seeking to hire a full-time Accountant to join its Office of Finance team. In this role, you will support the financial administration of philanthropic, endowment, and gift-funded programs that advance groundbreaking research, education, and clinical initiatives. Key responsibilities include:
Manage financial activity for foundation, endowment, gift, and other designated funds
Review and process expenditures, transfers, interdepartmental recharge transactions, deposits, and procurement requests
Reconcile financial ledgers and analyze account activity to ensure accuracy and compliance
Prepare monthly financial reports, forecasts, variance analyses, and year-end financial documentation
Monitor fund balances and projections to identify and prevent overdrafts
Process gift-related transactions and coordinate with appropriate campus offices regarding donor contributions
Assist with budget development, financial data collection, and special financial projects
Serve as resource to faculty and staff regarding account status, financial policies, and funding utilization
Knowledge of generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) and financial accounting practices
Knowledge of UCLA financial systems, policies, and procedures
Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, including the ability to create spreadsheets, perform data analysis, and generate reports
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple assignments, and consistency meet deadlines
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to establish effective working relationships with faculty, staff, vendors, and campus partners
